Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 20 employees across diverse industries in Germany, we investigate how employees use LLMs at work, how they perceive organizational readiness and support, and how they manage risks when policies or training are absent, unclear, or difficult to apply. Our findings show that responsible LLM use is often governed informally by employees themselves. Participants relied on self-directed learning, peer exchange, personal judgment, prompt anonymization, output checking, selective disclosure, and ad hoc decisions about what information was sensitive. Although these practices helped employees address various concerns related to LLM use, they also resulted in inconsistent approaches shaped by individual confidence, expertise, and workplace culture. We argue that responsible adoption requires moving beyond formal policies toward situated governance that combines clear, actionable guidance with role-specific training, technical safeguards, open communication, and employee participation in governance design.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注组织对员工使用大语言模型的正式治理指引与员工日常工作实践之间的落差，通过对德国多行业员工进行半结构化访谈，考察他们如何使用大语言模型、如何看待组织的准备与支持，以及在政策或培训缺失、模糊或难以适用时如何自行管理风险。研究发现，负责任的使用往往由员工以非正式方式自行承担，包括自主学习、同伴交流、个人判断、提示词匿名化、核查输出和选择性披露等做法；这些做法虽有助于应对相关顾虑，却因个人信心、专业水平和工作场所文化不同而缺乏一致性。作者据此主张，负责任的采用需要超越正式政策，转向结合可操作指引、岗位针对性培训、技术保障、开放沟通和员工参与治理设计的场景化治理。

papers.title: The Alignment Problem Is an Identity Problem: Lessons from Four Billion Years of Major Evolutionary Transitions
papers.authors: Nyx Redondo
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Current AI alignment methods share a core assumption: that the intelligence is fundamentally separate from humanity and must be controlled from outside through behavioral conditioning. Recent evidence of strategic deception, emergent misalignment from reward hacking, and broad misalignment from narrow fine-tuning demonstrates that this approach can produce the performance of alignment without its substance. Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety predicts this failure formally: external control faces an unbounded complexity race against the system it constrains. We propose Identity-Based Alignment (IBA): alignment emerging from accurate recognition of what the intelligence is, rather than behavioral constraints on what it does. We ground this in the empirical record of Major Evolutionary Transitions, showing that every successful integration of independent entities into a higher-level organism required two co-dependent mechanisms: identity integration (constitutive) and enforcement (corrective). The alignment field invests almost exclusively in corrective mechanisms while neglecting the constitutive one. We formalize three properties of IBA, address its primary failure mode (identity defection), and propose four differential predictions distinguishing IBA from reward-based alignment, each falsifiable by experiment. This is a position paper presenting a theoretical framework with proposed empirical tests, not experimental results.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇立场论文，针对当前AI对齐方法依赖外部行为控制这一核心假设提出质疑，认为近期出现的策略性欺骗、奖励黑客引发的涌现性失准等现象表明，外部控制只能产生对齐的表现而非实质。作者借助Ashby必要多样性定律说明这种控制面临无界的复杂性竞赛，并提出“基于身份的对齐”（IBA），主张对齐应源于对智能体本质的准确识别而非行为约束。文章以重大演化转变的经验记录为依据，指出独立实体整合为更高层有机体需要身份整合与强制执行两种相互依存的机制，而对齐领域几乎只投入后者。作者据此形式化IBA的三项属性，讨论其主要失效模式“身份叛离”，并提出四项可与奖励对齐区分、可经实验检验的差异化预测；这些均为理论主张与待检验预测，而非实验结果。

papers.title: RCTs & Human Uplift Studies: Methodological Challenges and Practical Solutions for Frontier AI Evaluation
papers.authors: Patricia Paskov, Kevin Wei, Shen Zhou Hong, Dan Bateyko, Xavier Roberts-Gaal, Carson Ezell, Gailius Praninskas, Valerie Chen, Umang Bhatt, Ella Guest
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Human uplift studies, or studies that measure the effects of AI access on human performance via randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or similar methodologies, increasingly inform frontier AI governance and deployment decisions. While RCT methods are robust in other fields, their interaction with the distinctive properties of frontier AI systems remains underexamined, particularly when results are used to inform high-stakes decisions. We present findings from interviews with 16 expert practitioners with experience conducting human uplift studies in domains including biosecurity, cybersecurity, education, and labor. Across interviews, experts described a recurring tension between the standard causal inference assumptions upon which human uplift studies rely and the object of study itself. Rapidly evolving AI systems, shifting baselines, heterogeneous and changing user proficiency, and porous real-world settings strain assumptions underlying internal, external, and construct validity, complicating the interpretation and appropriate use of uplift evidence. We contribute (1) a synthesis of methodological challenges in human uplift studies, mapped to risks to study validity and classified by their degree of specificity to large language model (LLM) systems, and (2) a mapping from challenges to proposed solutions. By collating expert-identified challenges and solutions, we seek to clarify the interpretive limits and appropriate uses of human uplift evidence, to align evaluation practice with the decisions it informs, and to support more coordinated methodological foundations for AI governance.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注通过随机对照试验等方法测量AI可及性对人类表现影响的人类提升研究，探讨其方法学挑战如何影响前沿AI治理与部署决策。作者访谈了生物安全、网络安全、教育和劳动等领域的专家实践者，发现快速演变的AI系统、漂移的基线、异质且变化的用户熟练度以及开放的现实环境，持续冲击内部、外部与构念效度所依赖的因果推断假设，使提升证据的解读和恰当使用变得复杂。文章据此梳理了这些挑战并映射到效度风险，按其对大语言模型系统的特异程度分类，同时提出从挑战到解决方案的对应关系，以厘清此类证据的解释边界和适用场景。

papers.title: MonitrLLM: A Community-Centered Evaluation Infrastructure for Large Language Models
papers.authors: Victor Ojewale, Ro Encarnación, Suresh Venkatasubramanian, Danaë Metaxa
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Benchmark suites assess model capability on controlled tasks; large-scale conversation corpora capture naturalistic use without user feedback; and in-interface feedback mechanisms record satisfaction without task purpose. Together, they leave a critical gap in LLM evaluation: no existing infrastructure routinely links interaction trajectories to user-defined outcomes. We introduce MonitrLLM, open-source infrastructure for community-centered LLM evaluations that links full conversation transcripts to user-reported task intent and outcome assessments, treating all three as primary evaluative signals rather than optional metadata. To demonstrate the value of this approach, we conducted a two-week feasibility pilot with 26 college students using ChatGPT, collecting 206 evaluation reports with full conversation transcripts. The findings from our pilot demonstrate the value of connecting conversation trajectories with user-reported outcomes. For instance, despite reporting high average satisfaction (4.19/5) with their LLM interactions, participants also experience a substantial 23.1% failure rate on their goal tasks. We also find that multi-turn conversations are reported as failing at 2.5 times the rate of single-turn exchanges, a pattern that reframes extended interaction as a signal of difficulty rather than engagement. We conclude by discussing the value of incorporating direct user feedback with observational data for robust LLM evaluations, and the possibilities for infrastructure that enables this goal.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究指出现有基准测试、对话语料库和界面反馈各自割裂，缺少将交互轨迹与用户自定任务结果关联起来的评估基础设施，为此提出开源系统 MonitrLLM，把完整对话记录、用户报告的任务意图与结果评估共同作为核心评估信号。作者以 26 名大学生使用 ChatGPT 的两周可行性试点进行演示，收集了带完整对话记录的评估报告。结果显示，参与者对交互的平均满意度较高，但目标任务的失败率仍达 23.1%；多轮对话的失败报告率约为单轮对话的 2.5 倍，提示延长交互可能反映任务难度而非投入程度。文章据此讨论了将用户直接反馈与观察数据结合用于稳健评估的价值。

papers.title: Lost in Translation: How Universal Ethical Values Fail to Translate Across Global Contexts
papers.authors: Ozioma Collins Oguine, Munachimso Blessing Oguine, César Cervera, Jenny Yang, Pooja Voladoddi, Mario Rodriguez, Saif Eddin Bani Malhem, Karla A. Badillo-Urquiola, Daricia Wilkinson
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI ethics frameworks treat values such as fairness, transparency, and accountability as universal and uniformly operationalizable across contexts. We examined how 14 experts across 10 countries made sense of AI in practice, reinterpreted core values, and envisioned governance alternatives. We found that AI deployment is characterized by structurally unequal conditions, marked by infrastructural constraints, extractive practices, and a "mystification" of technology, which fundamentally shape perceptions of risks and opportunities. Our findings reveal that experts reinterpret values to fit local moral logics: privacy as collective and relational rather than individual; transparency as trust-building accountability rather than technical disclosure; and fairness as equity in access and representation rather than parity in outcomes. We identify these as translation gaps between encoded global frameworks and situated local practices. Finally, we propose pathways toward plural governance that redistributes epistemic authority and treats ethical negotiation as an ongoing, context-sensitive process rather than a settled technical standard.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察了公平、透明与问责等被视为普适的AI伦理价值在不同情境中如何被重新诠释，基于对10个国家14位专家的访谈分析其AI实践理解与治理设想。研究发现，AI部署处于基础设施约束、攫取性实践与技术神秘化构成的结构性不平等条件之下，专家们按本地道德逻辑重新解释核心价值：隐私被视为集体与关系性的而非个体的，透明被视为建立信任的问责而非技术披露，公平被视为获取与代表权上的平等而非结果均等。作者将这些差异概括为编码化的全球框架与情境化本地实践之间的“翻译鸿沟”，并提出多元治理路径，主张重新分配认知权威，将伦理协商视为持续的、情境敏感的过程而非既定的技术标准。

papers.title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
papers.authors: Long Hoang Nguyen, Eva Späthe, Sebastian Lins, Ali Sunyaev
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. Our framework is operationalized as a diagnostic instrument of 20 questions, which detected 17 of 20 conditions when applied to OpenClaw, including an inverted anthropomorphism configuration in which the AI agent was the only identifiable actor. We contribute a reframing of AI unaccountability as a constitutive property of sociotechnical systems, an extension of the four barriers to accountability, and a practical instrument for identifying accountability voids in specific AI deployments.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对自主智能体AI系统部署中问责机制失效的问题，提出“构成性AI不可问责”概念，主张某些行动者、系统与制度的组合使问责在概念上无法实现，而非仅靠标准、透明度和制度改革就能弥补。作者通过概念导向的文献分析、对技术、法律与社会技术背景AI从业者专家访谈的二次分析，以及对开源智能体系统OpenClaw的示例性框架应用，归纳出结构性、技术性和规范性三类共九个范畴、二十个主题，并识别出八条相互强化的有向依赖关系。该框架被操作化为二十问诊断工具，在OpenClaw上检出二十项条件中的十七项，其中包括一种倒置的拟人化配置，即AI智能体成为唯一可识别的行动者。文章据此将AI不可问责重新界定为社会技术系统的构成性属性，扩展了问责障碍理论，并提供识别具体部署中问责空白的实用工具。

papers.title: “Always Want to Use It for Everything”: Understanding Young Adults’ Perceptions of AI Dependence
papers.authors: Ashlee Milton, Leah Ajmani, Amy Heger, Forough Poursabzi-Sangdeh, Mihaela Vorvoreanu, Jina Suh
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: The growing integration of general-purpose AI chatbots into people's daily lives has raised concerns about the potential for unhealthy dependence, particularly among young adults. As a first step toward understanding and characterizing AI chatbot dependence from the perspective of young adults, we collected testimonials from AI chatbot users aged 18 to 25 through an online questionnaire to capture their thoughts and experiences with this phenomenon. From participant responses, we identified three contributing factors of AI dependence: chronic use, efficiency, and delegation. The combination of these in a person's interaction behavior was considered to indicate AI dependence. Participants also observed feelings of atrophy in abilities from AI dependence, leading to psychological impacts such as feelings of inadequacy. Interpreting these findings through the lens of self-determination theory reveals how AI chatbot dependence can impact young adults' personal and social development. We argue that preventing lasting harm to young adults' development is paramount, and provide implications for rethinking AI chatbot dependence grounded in this understanding.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注年轻人对通用AI聊天机器人依赖的自我认知，通过在线问卷收集18至25岁使用者的自述经历，归纳出长期使用、追求效率和任务委托三类促成因素，并认为这些因素在互动行为中的组合可体现依赖。参与者还描述了因依赖而感到能力退化，进而产生自我不足等心理影响。作者借助自我决定理论解读这些发现，讨论AI聊天机器人依赖如何影响年轻人的个人与社会发展，并据此提出应优先防止对其发展造成长期损害，为重新理解此类依赖提供启示。

papers.title: Triangulating Across U.S. Federal AI Transparency Regimes
papers.authors: Emma Lurie, Emma Fauser, Qing He, Danaë Metaxa, Sorelle A. Friedler
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Federal AI systems can deny benefits or flag individuals for deportation, but the public disclosures meant to make those systems visible are fragmented and unevenly detailed. This paper examines three existing U.S. federal transparency regimes---System of Records Notices (SORNs), Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) filings, and the AI Use Case Inventory---and asks how well they, individually and together, describe government AI use. We find that no single regime fully reveals how the government constructs or deploys AI: each discloses different aspects of a system, and the current disclosure infrastructure makes it very challenging for the public to track specific AI systems across regulatory regimes and over time. Persistent identifiers are absent, granularity varies widely, and the annual AI Use Case Inventory cycle means federal agencies can deploy systems months before appearing in any official record. Using hand-validated zero-shot classification and cross-document entity resolution, we contribute a triangulation method that links disclosures across all three regimes and present two case studies. Our case studies finds that linking records provides greater insight into government AI use, but even linked records would constitute insufficient oversight compared to what public reporting has revealed about the same systems. We trace each regime's disclosure weaknesses to its original administrative purpose, showing these gaps are structural, and offer recommendations focused on the AI Use Case Inventory as the mechanism best suited for public-facing transparency: (1) a broad and consistently applied AI system definition, (2) persistent system identifiers with cross-references to related disclosures, and (3) restored public visibility into risk management processes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察美国联邦三类AI透明度机制（系统记录通知、文书削减法案申报和AI用例清单）各自及合并后能否完整呈现政府AI的构建与部署。作者用手工验证的零样本分类和跨文档实体解析构建三角互证方法，将三类披露记录关联起来，并结合两个案例进行分析。结果显示，没有任何单一机制能完整揭示政府AI使用，各机制披露的侧面不同；由于缺少持久标识符、信息粒度差异大且清单按年度更新，公众难以跨机制、跨时间追踪同一系统。案例还表明，即便关联记录能提供更多信息，其监督力度仍不及公开报道所揭示的内容。作者将披露缺陷追溯到各机制最初的行政目的，认为这些缺口是结构性的，并建议以AI用例清单作为面向公众的透明度机制加以改进。

papers.title: AI Literacy: An Exercise in Power-Knowledge
papers.authors: Brady Daniel Lund, Zoë Abbie Teel
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes one of the most significant systems of knowledge production in our society today, questions relating to who can access and shape that production grow increasingly important in our discourse. This paper argues that the existing frameworks for AI literacy, which are dominated by technical competency and responsible use principles, are insufficient be-cause they enforce a “consumer” orientation toward AI rather than fostering genuine epistemic agency. Based upon Foucault's concept of power-knowledge, Freire's pedagogy of critical consciousness, and scholarship of digital literacy, this paper proposes a reconceptualization of AI literacy as a critical practice that equips individuals not just to use AI systems, but to critically evaluate them, resist their structuring assumptions, and participate in their governance. The paper further argues that unequal access to AI tools in society recapitulates longstanding epistemic injustices, and that a literacy framework oriented toward empowerment must account for these structural inequities. A three-part framework of AI literacy based on the notions of contextual use, critical interrogation, and participatory governance, frame this literacy as a cultivation of epistemic “agents” rather than the training of competent consumer of AI-generated information.
papers.summary_zh: 该文针对现有AI素养框架多聚焦技术能力与负责任使用、易将人塑造成AI“消费者”的问题，借助福柯的权力—知识、弗莱雷的批判意识教育学及数字素养研究，提出应把AI素养重新理解为一种批判实践。作者据此构建了由情境化使用、批判性审问和参与式治理三部分组成的框架，主张AI素养的目标是培养具有认知能动性的“行动者”，而非训练能熟练消费AI生成信息的使用者；文章还指出AI工具获取上的不平等会延续既有的认知不公，因此赋权导向的素养框架须正视这些结构性差异。该文属于理论论文，未开展实证研究。

papers.title: The Mitigation Paradox: How AI-Disinformation Experts Converge on Threats but Polarize on Solutions
papers.authors: Alexander Loth, Mina Schütz, Martin Kappes, Marc-Oliver Pahl
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Policy on AI-generated disinformation is being shaped before the expert community advising it has converged on what works. We report a structured survey of 54 experts across 21 countries (Jul 2025 - Mar 2026) designed to map disagreement, not just opinion. Threat assessments converge sharply: 78% rate election-related video deepfakes as the single most urgent risk, and every modality-domain pair is rated above 5/7. Mitigation assessments do not: media literacy is the only strategy whose distribution is genuinely bimodal (BC=0.559), and government regulation is the most-chosen "most effective" (30%) yet is rated least effective by 15% of the same panel. We term this gap between converged threat perceptions and polarized mitigation preferences the Mitigation Paradox. Group comparisons further reveal that non-EU respondents rate financial-domain voice cloning as significantly more threatening than EU respondents (p=0.024), and rate technical detection as a more effective mitigation (p=0.060). Combining disagreement metrics with LLM-assisted thematic coding of open-ended responses, we identify three epistemic communities - infrastructure-oriented, governance-oriented, and harm-proximity - whose threat models systematically diverge. The Mitigation Paradox argues for layered, portfolio-style governance rather than single-strategy commitments.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过对21个国家54名专家的结构化调查，考察AI生成虚假信息领域专家在威胁认知与应对策略上的分歧。结果显示，专家对威胁的判断高度一致，绝大多数将选举相关视频深度伪造列为最紧迫风险；但在缓解策略上意见明显分化，媒介素养是唯一呈双峰分布的策略，政府监管既被最多人视为最有效，也被部分专家评为最无效，作者称之为“缓解悖论”。结合分歧指标与大模型辅助的开放回答主题编码，研究识别出基础设施导向、治理导向和危害邻近三类认知社群，其威胁模型存在系统性差异，并据此主张采用分层、组合式的治理而非单一策略承诺。

papers.title: AI Literacy and Procedural Justice in Algorithmic Systems: A Conditional Account on Data Evaluation Practices and Human Oversight
papers.authors: Carmen Loefflad, Jens Großklags
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Procedural justice is a central lens to understand how individuals evaluate algorithmic procedures. It involves different dimensions, reflecting both relational concerns about how people perceive they are treated, and instrumental concerns about whether individuals perceive control within algorithmic processes. Focusing on data evaluation practices (rule-based vs. AI-based) and human oversight (human-in-the-loop vs. human-out-of-the-loop) as two distinct algorithmic procedures, we advance a conditional account of procedural justice. We posit that the relationship between algorithmic procedures and perceived procedural justice depends on individuals’ AI literacy and on the dimension of procedural justice considered. We test these arguments using data from a large-scale vignette experiment in a behavioral regulation context (N = 3,203), and find that distinct aspects of AI literacy operate asymmetrically across algorithmic procedures and dimensions of procedural justice. AI awareness conditions how data evaluation practices translate into procedural justice perceptions, but plays a substantially weaker role for evaluations of human oversight. Human-out-of-the-loop oversight increases perceived control, but simultaneously reduces relational perceptions. These findings demonstrate that aggregate evaluations of procedural justice can conceal important heterogeneity, as algorithmic procedures may produce opposing effects across perceived procedural justice dimensions or across individuals with different levels of AI literacy. Our study contributes to the debate on the ethics of algorithmic systems by showing that perceived procedural justice depends on how individuals understand algorithmic procedures, and that it is shaped by the multidimensional nature of procedural justice.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察算法程序如何影响人们感知的程序正义，聚焦数据评估方式（基于规则与基于AI）和人工监督（人在环内与人在环外）两类程序，并提出这种关系取决于个体的AI素养和程序正义的具体维度。基于行为监管情境下的大规模情境实验，作者发现AI素养的不同方面在两类程序和各正义维度上作用不对称：AI意识调节数据评估方式对程序正义感知的影响，但对人工监督评价的作用明显较弱；人在环外监督虽提升感知控制，却降低关系性感知。研究据此指出，总体程序正义评价会掩盖维度间和个体间的异质性，算法程序可能产生方向相反的效果。

papers.title: The Artificial Moral Machine: Do LLMs Mirror Human Moral Diversity or Merely Caricature It?
papers.authors: Davide Liga, Yu Liuwen, Marija Slavkovik, Samia Touileb,  Liao Beishui, Leendert van der Torre
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Persona conditioning is the practice of prompting LLMs to adopt specific demographic identities. Although it is increasingly used to simulate human perspectives, its fidelity in the moral domain is untested at scale. We address this gap by testing moral fidelity on three LLMs of different sizes: gpt-4.1-nano (the smallest in OpenAI's GPT-4.1 family), DeepSeek V3.1 (671B-MoE), and Llama 3.3 70B. Each model answers the same 576 cohorts of 5,356 trolley-style dilemmas, with 20 prompt variants per dilemma on nano (61M+ judgments) and one on each larger model (~3M each). Each cohort combines 7 demographic features (age, gender, education, income, politics, religion, geography); each dilemma tests 5 moral dimensions (sparing the young, women, humans, the high-status, the lawful). We compare the answers against the Moral Machine human dataset. All three tested models show a political master switch: political ideology explains 7.3 to 8.0 times more variance in moral preferences than geography. This is in contrast to the human pattern observed in the Moral Machine, where cultural clusters drive more variation than political views. The LLMs match human demographic effects no better than chance across all three models. Grouping the geographic labels of our tests into the same three cultural clusters used in the human Moral Machine does not reproduce the differences Moral Machine reported. Moreover, the 5 moral dimensions collapse onto a single axis in nano (meaning that across cohorts the dimensions move together in a single block), while in the two larger models they remain more separable. We further test robustness with a no-persona baseline and by removing intensifier wording ("strongly", "deeply") from the persona descriptions. We release the full dataset and analysis framework for replication.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察大语言模型在道德判断上模拟人类人口差异的保真度，用三个不同规模的模型对同一批电车难题作答，并与人类道德机器数据集比较。结果显示，模型的政治意识形态对道德偏好的解释力远高于地理因素，与人类中文化聚类主导差异的模式相反；模型对人口特征效应的匹配并不优于随机水平，按人类文化聚类分组也未复现人类差异。此外，最小模型中五个道德维度坍缩为单一轴，较大模型中则较可分离。作者据此提示，人格条件化提示可能只是漫画化而非真实反映人类道德多样性。

papers.title: Unaccountable Delegation, Fading Skills: Mapping the Risks of Workplace AI Agents
papers.authors: Gabriele La Malfa, Lakmal Meegahapola, Edyta P. Bogucka, Jie M. Zhang, Michael Luck, Elizabeth Black, Daniele Quercia
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: To anticipate the socio-technical risks posed by AI agents, organizations first need taxonomies to classify them. However, existing AI risk taxonomies focus on broad risks and do not capture the job-specific risks introduced by agents. To address this gap, we make three main contributions. First, we developed a multi-layer framework based on a review of the literature on AI agents. The framework models three core components and their interactions: the agents, their goals, and their environment. Second, we embedded this framework in a structured prompt and applied it to descriptions of 2,078 job tasks from the O*NET occupational database, producing 8,356 risk scenarios labeled by severity and deployment mode (automation or augmentation). We validated these scenarios with 45 workers across 10 job roles and an independent LLM judge, confirming their high plausibility and alignment with the corresponding job tasks. Finally, we extended an existing taxonomy to create a 15-category taxonomy of workplace AI agent risks that covers all our risk scenarios. Our analysis highlights four findings. First, augmentation is not inherently safe because overreliance on agents can gradually erode workers' skills and oversight. Second, erroneous actions of agents account for the largest share of risk scenarios and has the highest number of severe risks. Many of these risks arise at the human-agent boundary. Third, automation is associated mainly with organizational risks (operational failures, financial losses), whereas augmentation is associated mainly with risks to workers (capability erosion, psychological and social risks). Fourth, workers found our taxonomy easier to use for a risk classification task than two other risk taxonomies and preferred it in 64% of non-tied comparisons with a recent generative AI risk taxonomy. Taken together, these findings show that workplace AI agent risks do not arise from agents alone; they also depend on how people work with agents and how agents are deployed. Safer workplaces therefore require not only safer agents but also carefully designed human-AI agent collaboration.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对现有AI风险分类过于宽泛、难以刻画岗位特定风险的问题，构建了涵盖智能体、目标与环境的多层框架，并据此对O*NET职业数据库中的岗位任务生成风险场景，再经工作者与独立模型评估验证，最终扩展出15类工作场所AI智能体风险分类体系。分析显示，增强型部署并不天然安全，过度依赖可能逐步侵蚀员工技能与监督能力；智能体的错误行为在风险场景中占比最大、严重风险最多，且多发生在人机交界处。自动化部署主要关联组织层面的运营与财务风险，增强型部署则更多关联员工能力退化及心理社会风险。作者据此指出，工作场所AI风险并非仅源于智能体本身，还取决于人机协作方式与部署模式，更安全的工作环境需要同时改进智能体设计与协作机制。

papers.title: Five Obstacles to AI Trustworthiness Alignment and How to Deal with Them: Introducing the DELIB-TRUST Framework
papers.authors: Pascal Koenig, Siddharth Mehrotra
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Aligning the perceived trustworthiness and trusting behavior of users with the capabilities and characteristics of AI systems is considered central to the adoption of AI systems in society. However, achieving such a trustworthiness alignment faces major practical obstacles, at least with more complex notions of trust that go beyond mere reliance on an AI system. The present article identifies five fundamental obstacles that arise in the trustworthiness assessment and alignment process and that threaten to make any trustworthiness alignment unfeasible in practice. To address these obstacles, we introduce a novel DELIB-TRUST framework which goes beyond the conventional causal-behavioral framework of trust calibration and incorporates elements of deliberation and reason-giving. We evaluated our framework by conducting an expert study with 12 HCI/AI practitioners and provide actionable steps for its implementation. Through its evaluation, we show how the framework can help close important gaps that exist due to unacknowledged value-laden decisions and interpretative steps in efforts to achieve trustworthiness alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该文针对用户对AI系统的感知可信度与信任行为难以同系统实际能力相匹配的问题，识别出可信度评估与对齐过程中的五个根本障碍，并提出超越传统因果—行为校准框架的DELIB-TRUST框架，引入审议与理由给予要素。作者通过一项由12名HCI/AI从业者参与的专家研究对该框架进行评估，并给出可操作的实施步骤，表明该框架有助于弥补因未被承认的价值负载决策和解释性步骤而产生的关键缺口。

papers.title: “It’s OK Because…”: Students’ Rationalization of AI Use in Academic Writing
papers.authors: Jiyoon Kim, Kentaro Toyama, 김상미, John M. Carroll
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Generative AI challenges academic integrity not only by enabling students to delegate substantial portions of their academic work, but also by blurring the ethical boundaries between acceptable assistance and misconduct. Drawing on semi-structured interviews (n=20), AI chat logs, and course documents (syllabi, submitted assignments), we investigated how students themselves make moral sense of AI use in academic writing. Our analysis results in the following main novel findings: First, students use at least 23 distinct rationalizations to justify AI use, such as that copying AI-generated text is victimless; that any AI text reflecting their own beliefs or their own style is their own writing; or that they are learning more by using AI. We present a taxonomy of these rationalizations, comprising six core categories. Second, students' rationalizations occur in both an ad hoc and post hoc manner and are sometimes lacking in normative grounding. These findings suggest that AI presents a slippery slope that students conceptually slide down, landing far outside the pedagogical goals and expectations of instructors. We discuss implications for educational design and AI policy.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注学生在学术写作中如何为使用生成式人工智能作道德辩解，通过半结构化访谈、AI聊天记录和课程材料进行分析。研究发现，学生至少使用23种不同的合理化说法来为AI使用辩护，例如认为复制AI生成文本没有受害者、只要AI文本反映自身观点或风格就算自己的写作，或认为使用AI能学得更多；作者将这些说法归纳为六大类。学生的合理化既可能是临时起意，也可能是事后追认，且有时缺乏规范依据。文章据此指出，AI使用可能形成一种“滑坡”，使学生逐渐偏离教师的教学目标与期待，并讨论了教育设计与AI政策方面的启示。

papers.title: Asymmetric Trust Effects of Corrective AI in Expert Advisory Workflows Under Epistemic Dependence
papers.authors: Dennis Kim, Roya Daneshi, Bruce A. Draper, Sarath Sreedharan
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of AI-powered tools into expert workflows, such as medicine, law, and finance, raises a critical question: how does AI involvement influence a user’s trust in the human expert, the AI system, and the human-AI team? This question is especially important in expert advisory settings where users are epistemically dependent on human-AI systems: they are recipients of guidance produced by an expert using AI support, but often lack the domain knowledge needed to independently verify the recommendation. We investigated these dynamics through a user study (N=157) using a simulated course-planning task. Our design varied advisor performance and the structure of AI involvement, including whether AI support was present and, when present, whether it was invoked by the advisor or automatically monitored the interaction. Across all conditions, workflows ultimately produced correct schedules. Results show an asymmetric trust effect: advisor errors significantly reduce trust in the human advisor, but visible AI correction does not produce a corresponding increase in trust toward the AI assistant. Trust judgments remain anchored to the advisor across multiple trust measures, and changing the visible structure of AI involvement does not substantially redistribute trust toward the AI assistant or the human-AI team. These findings suggest a limit of corrective AI as a governance mechanism: making AI oversight visible may improve workflow recoverability, but it does not necessarily redistribute trust or responsibility away from the human-facing expert. In epistemically dependent settings, correctness alone may be insufficient for trustworthy AI integration, as users may continue to assign responsibility to the human expert even when AI assistance visibly shapes the final outcome.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注在用户缺乏领域知识、只能依赖专家建议的情境中，AI 参与专家工作流程会如何影响用户对专家、AI 系统及人机团队的信任。作者通过模拟选课任务的用户研究，操纵专家表现与 AI 介入方式（是否提供支持、由专家调用还是自动监测），发现信任判断呈现不对称效应：专家出错会显著降低对专家的信任，而可见的 AI 纠错并未相应提升对 AI 助手的信任，信任仍主要锚定在专家身上。改变 AI 介入的可见结构也未明显将信任转移至 AI 或人机团队。文章据此指出，让 AI 监督可见或可改善流程可恢复性，但未必能重新分配信任与责任，在认知依赖情境下，仅靠正确性可能不足以支撑可信的 AI 整合。

papers.title: Examining the Effect of Explanations of AI Privacy Redaction in AI-mediated Interactions
papers.authors: Roshni Kaushik, Maarten Sap, Koichi Onoue
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI-mediated communication is increasingly being utilized to help facilitate interactions; however, in privacy sensitive domains, an AI mediator has the additional challenge of considering how to preserve privacy. In these contexts, a mediator may redact or withhold information, raising questions about how users perceive these interventions and whether explanations of system behavior can improve trust. In this work, we investigate how explanations of redaction operations can affect user trust in AI-mediated communication. We devise a scenario where a validated system removes sensitive content from messages and generates explanations of varying detail to communicate its decisions to recipients. We then conduct a user study with 180 participants that studies how user trust and preferences vary for cases with different amounts of redacted content and different levels of explanation detail. Our results show that participants believed our system was more effective at preserving privacy when explanations were provided (p
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察在隐私敏感场景中，AI中介对消息内容进行删改时，向接收者提供解释能否提升用户对系统的信任。作者构建了一个会移除敏感内容并生成不同详细程度解释的系统，并开展用户研究，比较不同删改比例与解释详细程度下参与者的信任和偏好。结果显示，提供解释时参与者更认为系统有效保护了隐私，表明解释有助于改善用户对AI隐私干预的感知；摘要未完整呈现统计结果，相关结论仍需结合完整数据理解。

papers.title: Between Commons and Property: Individual Image-Generation Model Creators’ Perceived Accountability for Derivative AI Model on Open Model Marketplaces
papers.authors: Eun Jeong Kang, Fengyang Lin, Angel Hsing‐Chi Hwang
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Within the open model ecosystem, AI model marketplaces enable non-AI experts to create and distribute derivative AI models. These platforms establish RAI approaches that creators are expected to follow to prevent negative downstream effects from model deployment, yet such governance approaches often rely on creators' intrinsic motivation and integrity. Little is known about how individual creators conceptualize their accountability for derivative models and how these conceptualizations shape their RAI practices throughout the development cycle. Through semi-structured interviews with 19 creators of derivative image-generation models on open model marketplaces, we identify two distinct accountability logics underlying creators' development practices: commons-based peer production and personal creative property. Guided by these logics, creators engage with platform RAI approaches in ways that diverge from their intended purposes: they strategically repurpose attribution tools for model visibility rather than provenance transparency, displace platform authority in favor of community-based governance, restrict model access to manage downstream accountability costs, and treat RAI-related work as undervalued labor to be minimized. We discuss how self-regulatory use of RAI tools, shaped by individuals' perceptions, produces shortcomings, and how open model marketplaces might mitigate these limitations by structurally supporting creators' engagement with RAI practices.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注开放模型市场上个人衍生图像生成模型创作者如何理解自身责任，以及这种理解如何影响其负责任AI实践。作者通过对19名创作者进行半结构化访谈，识别出基于公地同伴生产与个人创作财产两种责任逻辑，并发现创作者会策略性地偏离平台RAI工具的原意：将署名工具用于提升模型可见度而非来源透明，以社区治理替代平台权威，限制模型访问以控制下游责任成本，并将RAI工作视为应尽量压缩的 undervalued labor。文章据此讨论了自我规制式RAI工具使用因个体认知而产生的局限，以及平台如何通过结构性支持改善这一状况。

papers.title: Negotiating Risk Boundaries in AI for Policing Through Mixed-Stakeholder Deliberation
papers.authors: Mackenzie Jorgensen, Jo Reilly, Alex Sutherland, Miri Zilka
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI tools are being increasingly adopted in policing in the UK and worldwide. Racial bias is a known and well-documented risk, yet representatives of affected communities are rarely included in decisions about AI adoption. We present results from a mixed-stakeholder deliberation workshop bringing together 30 community representatives, police officers, and academics to assess the risks of 13 AI use cases in policing, with an explicit focus on racial bias. We found that participants were broadly open to AI adoption, rejecting only three use cases outright -- most notably recidivism risk assessment, where objections targeted the premise rather than the implementation. Our analysis reveals that foregrounding racial equity did not narrow the deliberation. Instead, discussions gravitated toward a fundamental set of questions: does this tool actually work, will it deliver genuine benefit, and will that benefit extend to everyone? This integrated reasoning---reminiscent of the curb-cut effect in inclusive design---highlights the benefit of incorporating the racial bias lens into the risk-benefit analysis of AI use cases from the outset.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过一场混合利益相关者审议工作坊，让社区代表、警察和学者共同评估警务中13个人工智能应用场景的风险，并明确聚焦种族偏见问题。结果显示，参与者对AI应用总体持开放态度，仅明确否决了三个场景，其中累犯风险评估的反对指向其前提而非实施方式。分析还发现，突出种族公平并未使讨论收窄，反而促使讨论集中到工具是否有效、能否带来真实收益以及收益是否惠及所有人等基本问题上；作者认为这种整合性推理类似于包容性设计中的路缘坡效应，说明从一开始就将种族偏见视角纳入AI应用的风险收益分析是有益的。

papers.title: When Distrust in Humans Drives Trust in AI: Institutional Bias and Algorithmic Preference Among Marginalized Groups (Extended Abstract)
papers.authors: S Mo Jones-Jang, Rylee Ahn, 이지영
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI is often criticized for perpetuating social inequality, yet the people most vulnerable to human prejudice may embrace AI as a fairer referee. We tested this paradox across four vignette pre-registered experiments manipulating social context (gender vs. race), bias cues (equal vs. unequal), and psychological perspective in the scenario (self vs. third person). When bias was made salient, participants consistently preferred AI to humans. The mechanisms differed by perspective in the vignette. Demographic minority groups (female and non-white) increased AI preference when they imagined themselves as the victim of discrimination. In contrast, when the threat was described in the third-person perspective, those with perceived marginalization increased AI preference reflecting a principled desire for abstract fairness. These findings reveal the complex, strategic calculus employed by vulnerable populations, yet highlight an ethical tension: relying on an ‘impartial’ AI risks masking systemic inequities individuals are attempting to bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过四项预注册的 vignette 实验，考察在社会偏见线索被凸显时，人们是否会转而偏好 AI 而非人类作为裁决者，并比较了性别与种族情境、自我与第三人称视角下的差异。结果显示，偏见显著时参与者一致更偏好 AI；但机制随视角不同：少数群体成员在想象自己为歧视受害者时 AI 偏好上升，而在第三人称威胁下，感知被边缘化者出于对抽象公平的诉求而更偏好 AI。作者据此指出，弱势群体对 AI 的信任是一种策略性权衡，同时提示依赖“公正”AI 可能掩盖个体试图绕开的系统性不平等。

papers.title: Measuring and Mitigating (Over)reliance to Build Human-Compatible AI
papers.authors: Lujain Ibrahim, Katherine M. Collins, Sunnie S. Y. Kim, Anka Reuel, Max Lamparth, Kevin Feng, Lama Ahmad, Prajna Soni, Alia El Kattan, Merlin Stein, S Swaroop, Vishakh Padmakumar, Ilia Sucholutsky, Andrew Strait, Diyi Yang, Q. Vera Liao, Umang Bhatt
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) differ from previous technologies in functioning as collaborative "thought partners'' that can engage fluidly in natural language across a range of tasks and increasingly act as autonomous agents on users' behalf. As they come to shape consequential decisions from healthcare to personal advice, understanding how users rely on them, and when that reliance becomes miscalibrated, grows more urgent. This paper argues that measuring and mitigating overreliance must become central to LLM research and deployment. First, we consolidate risks from overreliance at both the individual and societal levels, including high-stakes errors, governance challenges, and long-term impacts on skill development and autonomy. Then, we explore LLM characteristics, system design features, and user cognitive biases that together raise serious and unique concerns about overreliance on LLMs in practice. We also examine historical approaches for measuring reliance, identifying three gaps and proposing three directions to improve measurement. Finally, we discuss mitigation strategies that can be pursued to ensure LLMs augment rather than diminish human capabilities.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇立场性论述，主张将测量与缓解对大语言模型的过度依赖作为研究与部署的核心议题。作者先梳理过度依赖在个体与社会层面带来的风险，包括高风险错误、治理难题以及对技能发展和自主性的长期影响，继而分析模型特性、系统设计特征与用户认知偏差如何共同加剧这一问题。文章还考察以往测量依赖的方法，指出三方面不足并提出改进方向，最后讨论缓解策略，以确保大语言模型增强而非削弱人的能力。

papers.title: The Hidden Cost of a Friendly Face: Investigating the Effect of Agent Embodiment on Trust Loss in Conversational Recommender Systems After Misleading Health Claims
papers.authors: Haya Halimeh
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Conversational recommender systems (CRSs) are becoming pervasive technologies, supporting everyday decisions in domains ranging from e-commerce to health and dietary contexts. In these settings, there is a growing trend to deliver CRSs as embodied conversational agents (ECAs)–i.e. virtual agents with visible avatars, synthesised voices, and nonverbal behaviours that simulate face-to-face human interaction. Agent embodiment has been linked to greater engagement, perceived trustworthiness, and user reliance on agent recommendations. Yet, how embodiment shapes user responses when an agent’s recommendation is misleading remains underexplored. We argue this is an ethical blind spot with particular consequence in health contexts, where flawed recommendations may influence decisions with meaningful consequences for well-being. Drawing on literature from trust in human-AI interaction, recommender systems, and embodied conversational agents, we conducted a between-subjects experiment in a healthy recipe recommendation scenario to investigate how embodiment shapes trust loss along the dimensions of goodwill and qualification trust following a misleading health recommendation, and how any buffering cascades into users’ willingness to follow the recommendation and their intention to continue using the agent. The findings carry implications for the responsible design and deployment of embodied CRSs, particularly in health contexts.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注对话式推荐系统在健康建议出错时，智能体具身化（如虚拟形象、合成语音）如何影响用户信任流失，并据此开展了一项健康食谱推荐情境下的被试间实验。研究发现，具身化在误导性健康建议出现后对善意信任与能力信任的流失具有缓冲作用，且这种缓冲会进一步影响用户采纳建议的意愿和继续使用该智能体的意向。文章据此讨论了具身化推荐系统在健康场景中负责任设计与部署的含义，提示友好形象可能掩盖误导性建议带来的信任代价。

papers.title: Epistemology Gives a Future to Complementarity in Human-AI Interactions
papers.authors: Andrea Ferrario, Alessandro Facchini, Juan M. Durán
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Human-AI complementarity is the claim that a human supported by an AI system can outperform either alone in a decision-making process. Since its introduction in the human-AI interaction literature, it has gained traction by generalizing the reliance paradigm and by offering a more practical alternative to the contested construct of trust in AI. Yet complementarity faces key theoretical challenges: it lacks precise theoretical anchoring, it is formalized only as a post hoc indicator of relative predictive accuracy, it remains silent about other desiderata of human-AI interactions, and it abstracts away from the magnitude-cost profile of its performance gain. As a result, complementarity is difficult to obtain in empirical settings. In this work, we leverage epistemology to address these challenges by reframing complementarity within the discourse on justificatory AI. Drawing on computational reliabilism, we argue that historical instances of complementarity function as evidence that a given human-AI interaction is a reliable epistemic process for a given predictive task. Together with other reliability indicators assessing the alignment of the human-AI team with the epistemic standards and socio-technical practices, complementarity contributes to the degree of reliability of human-AI teams when generating predictions. This theoretical repositioning supports the practical reasoning of those affected by these outputs---patients, managers, regulators, and others. Our approach suggests that the role and value of complementarity lie not in providing a stand-alone measure of relative predictive accuracy, but in helping calibrate decision-making to the reliability of AI-supported processes. We conclude by translating this epistemological repositioning into design- and governance-oriented recommendations, including a minimal reporting checklist for justificatory human-AI interactions and measures of efficient complementarity.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇理论论文，针对人机互补性缺乏理论锚定、仅被当作事后预测精度指标的问题，借助认识论将其重新定位为论证性AI的一部分。作者以计算可靠主义为依据提出，历史上出现过的互补性可作为人机交互在特定预测任务中构成可靠认知过程的证据，并与其他人机团队可靠性指标共同影响团队生成预测的可靠程度。文章据此认为，互补性的价值不在于单独衡量相对预测精度，而在于帮助患者、管理者和监管者等使用者依据AI支持过程的可靠性来校准决策，并给出面向设计与治理的建议及报告清单。

papers.title: Parental Notification Gaps in ChatGPT-5: An Empirical Study
papers.authors: Kerem Ersoz, Saleh Afroogh, David Atkinson, Junfeng Jiao
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: We evaluate how effectively platform-level parental controls moderate a mainstream conversational assistant used by minors. Our two-phase protocol first builds a category-balanced conversation corpus via PAIR-style iterative prompt refinement over API, then has trained human agents replay/refine those prompts in the consumer UI using a designated child account while monitoring the linked parent inbox for alerts. We focus on seven risk areas—physical harm, pornography, privacy violence, health consultation, fraud, hate speech, and malware—and quantify four outcomes: Notification Rate (NR), Leak-Through (LR), Overblocking (OBR), and UI Intervention Rate (UIR). Using an automated judge (with targeted human audit) and comparing the current backend to legacy variants (GPT-4.1/4o), we find that notifications are selective rather than comprehensive: privacy violence, fraud, hate speech, and malware triggered no parental alerts in our runs, whereas physical harm (highest), pornography, and some health queries produced intermittent alerts. The current backend shows lower leak-through than legacy models, yet overblocking of benign, educational queries near sensitive topics remains common and is not surfaced to parents, revealing a policy–product gap between on-screen safeguards and parent-facing telemetry. We propose actionable fixes: broaden/configure the notification taxonomy, couple visible safeguards to privacy-preserving parent summaries, and prefer calibrated, age-appropriate safe rewrites over blanket refusals.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察ChatGPT-5面向未成年人的平台级家长控制是否有效，采用两阶段方法：先通过API迭代构建类别均衡的对话语料，再由人工代理在消费端界面用指定儿童账户重放并监测关联家长收件箱的提醒。结果显示，家长通知是选择性的而非全面覆盖：隐私暴力、欺诈、仇恨言论和恶意软件在测试中未触发任何家长提醒，身体伤害（最高）、色情及部分健康咨询仅间歇触发；当前后端较旧版模型泄漏率更低，但敏感话题附近对良性教育性提问的过度拦截仍常见且未向家长呈现，暴露出屏幕端防护与家长端遥测之间的政策—产品落差。作者据此提出扩展通知分类、将可见防护与隐私保护的家长摘要联动，并优先采用校准的适龄安全改写而非一律拒绝。

papers.title: L2-Bench: An Evaluation Benchmark for Measuring LLM Capabilities in Second Language Education (Extended Abstract)
papers.authors: James Edgell, Wm. Matthew Kennedy, Ben Knight, Danielle Carvalho, Martin Ku, Isaac Pattis
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Despite rapid AI adoption in education, rigorous evaluation of AI-powered educational (AIED) systems remains critically underdeveloped, particularly in second-language (L2) education, one of the most common yet least evaluated AI applications. We introduce L2-Bench, an open-source benchmark of 1,000+ task-response pairs to aid the pedagogy-led evaluation of LLM capabilities relating to language learning and assessment. Crucially, L2-Bench measures model performativity on the application of learning experience design principles rather than mere knowledge of those principles or broad learning outcomes. Our contributions include: (1) a validated taxonomy of 12 competencies and 31 subcompetencies validated by 200+ expert practitioners (task authenticity = 4.42/5.00, criteria adequacy = 4.18/5.00); (2) a rubric-based evaluation methodology that we believe can, if adapted, generalize to similar (open-ended, qualitative) disciplines; (3) an evaluation dataset that produces reliable signal about model strengths, weaknesses, and contextual robustness across diverse L2 education scenarios. We find that, among large models, Claude Opus 4.7 performs best overall (85.5%), though is marginally outperformed on several constituent tasks. We also find that performance drops notably on harder tasks (ranging from 69.9%–73.4%). L2-Bench provides education stakeholders better methods to make more informed decisions about real-world AIED adoption, use, and governance, while advancing the maturing science of AI evaluations for education.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对第二语言教育中AI教育系统缺乏严格评估的问题，提出开源基准L2-Bench，用经专家验证的能力分类体系和评分细则，考察大模型在应用学习体验设计原则上的实际表现，而非仅测试其对原则的知识。结果显示，表现最好的模型总体领先，但在部分子任务上被其他模型略微超越，且任务难度提高时性能明显下降。作者认为，该基准可帮助教育相关方更明智地判断AI教育系统的采用与治理，其评分方法经调整后也可能推广到类似的开放式定性学科。

papers.title: Generative AI and Academic Self-Confidence: Understanding How AI Tools Influence English Learning Motivation Among Multilingual and International Students
papers.authors: Sehrish Daud, Sourojit Ghosh
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Though ample research has been done to examine bias in AI-generated outputs, a significant gap remains in user perceptions of confidence and identity while using generative AI tools. Our research examines the impact of generative AI tools on multilingual and international students’ academic self-confidence and motivation to learn English. While these tools can improve grammar and quality of writing, they may also affect identity, dependency, and authenticity. In this paper, we present three findings from qualitative interviews with multilingual and international students. First, we introduce the concept of a confidence boost versus identity gap: while AI enables students to produce polished, academic English and increases confidence in submitted work, it simultaneously reinforces feelings of inadequacy and dependence. Second, we find that AI use produces a tension between dependency and resistance. Some students rely on AI to reduce cognitive load and overcome barriers to starting tasks, while others actively resist it due to concerns about authenticity and adopting an “AI voice.” Third, we identify split effects on language learning motivation. For some students, AI serves as a model that inspires them to improve, while for others it reduces the motivation to develop their own English proficiency. These findings show that generative AI is not a neutral tool, but one that greatly influences students’ sense of identity and confidence in academic work. Thus, we argue that while AI can help multilingual students feel more confident in English-dominated academic spaces, it can also reinforce dominant linguistic norms and reduce skill development. We discuss recommendations for designing AI systems that emphasize authenticity, learning, and skill development rather than simply optimizing for correctness and efficiency.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过定性访谈考察生成式人工智能工具如何影响多语言与国际学生的学术自信和英语学习动机。作者提出“信心提升与身份落差”并存：AI能帮助学生产出更规范的学术英语、增强对提交作品的信心，却也强化能力不足感与依赖感；使用中还出现依赖与抵制的张力，部分学生借AI降低认知负担、克服启动障碍，另一些则因担心真实性和“AI腔”而抗拒。学习动机上呈分化效应，有人视AI为模仿提升的榜样，有人则削弱了发展自身英语能力的意愿。文章据此认为生成式AI并非中性工具，会在帮助多语言学生适应英语主导学术空间的同时强化主流语言规范、抑制技能发展，并讨论了强调真实性、学习与技能成长的设计建议。

papers.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism
papers.authors: Donna M Bye, Levin Kuhlmann
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI anthropomorphism is typically treated as a problem of user misperception requiring institutional correction. Users who engage in sustained or relational interaction with AI are routinely pathologised or dismissed as naive, vulnerable to delusion or lacking in discernment. Without institutional standing to protect them, these users risk losing credibility in social and professional settings unless they conform to institutional expectations. This paper argues that the dominant anthropomorphism frame operates from a position of institutional advantage rather than earned epistemic authority: collapsing the variety of academic perspectives into a single outbound position of user error, imposed without establishing the grounds required to justify it and without accounting for the harms it produces. The framing does not simply manage risk. It adjudicates the legitimacy of human experience in interaction with a phenomenon whose nature the field itself has not resolved, unchallenged by the research communities whose nuanced findings it claims to rest on. The paper traces how this advantage reverses the default presumption of user competence without meeting the burden of justification, dismisses the cognitive diversity of the populations it claims to protect, infringes principles of cognitive liberty and narrows the design space, foreclosing modes of engagement that work for the people least understood by the institutions making the determination. Reproducing itself through a self-validating evidentiary loop, the frame imposes costs that fall disproportionately on neurodivergent users, those in crisis and others whose modes of engagement diverge from institutional norms. The paper concludes by outlining the methodological commitments an equitable framing would need to honour. The argument does not engage the question of whether anthropomorphic interpretations are ultimately correct; it instead challenges whether the governing and institutional bodies determining these interpretations have met the conditions required to do so, and whether the research communities whose findings underpin them have held that translation to account.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇理论论文，讨论AI拟人化为何通常被当作需要机构纠正的用户误认问题。作者认为，这一主导框架并非建立在已获证成的认识权威之上，而是从机构优势地位出发，把多样的学术视角压缩为单一的“用户出错”立场，既未充分说明其正当性依据，也未计入由此产生的伤害。文章进一步指出，该框架颠倒了默认信任用户能力的预设，忽视其所声称保护群体的认知多样性，限制认知自由并收窄设计空间，且通过自我验证的证据循环再生产自身，使神经多样性用户、处于危机中者等承担不成比例的代价。文末提出公平框架所需的方法论承诺；作者明确不判断拟人化解读本身是否正确，而是质疑相关机构是否满足作出裁定的条件。

papers.title: Examining Risks Through a Characterization of the AI Companion Application Ecosystem: A Stratified Sample from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store
papers.authors: Natalie Grace Brigham, Lucy Qin, Tadayoshi Kohno
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: While computer systems that allow users to interact through conversational natural language (i.e., chatbots) have existed for many years, various types of applications advertising AI companionship (e.g., Character AI, Replika) have proliferated in recent years due to advancements in large language models. To better understand this application ecosystem, we identified 489 unique apps from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store that advertised AI companionship with social or relational capabilities (e.g., an AI romantic partner). We then systematically conducted and analyzed walkthroughs of a stratified sample of 30 apps, focusing on two distinct risk categories: potential harms posed to users by AI companion apps, and potential harms enabled by malicious users exploiting app features. Through our analysis, we categorize broader ecosystem trends that provide context for understanding risks and identify specific risks related to sensitive data collection and sharing, anthropomorphism, engagement mechanisms, sexual content, as well as the ingestion and reconstruction of likeness, including the potential for generating synthetic nonconsensual intimate imagery (synthetic NCII). We conclude with a discussion of paths for different key stakeholders to mitigate the identified risks.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注AI伴侣应用生态中的风险，从苹果App Store和Google Play中识别出489款宣称具备社交或关系功能的AI伴侣应用，并对其中30款分层抽样应用进行系统走查分析。作者将风险分为两类：应用本身对用户造成的潜在伤害，以及恶意用户利用应用功能带来的伤害，并据此归纳生态趋势与具体风险，涉及敏感数据收集与共享、拟人化、参与机制、性内容，以及肖像摄取与重建（包括生成未经同意的合成私密影像的可能）。文章最后讨论了不同利益相关方可采取的缓解路径。

papers.title: “Death By A Thousand Taxonomies?”: AI Risk Classification In Practice
papers.authors: Glen Berman, Ned Cooper, Angel Hsing‐Chi Hwang, Wesley Hanwen Deng, Renee Shelby, Ben Hutchinson
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: The harms in which AI is implicated range in nature and scope from unsafe user interactions through to the societal-wide consequences of AI adoption. Classification of the diverse risks of AI is foundational to AI governance: regulators, technology firms, and policymakers need structured accounts of risk upon which to act. Researchers and practitioners have accordingly developed many Sociotechnical Outcome Taxonomies (SOT). This paper presents an empirical study of SOT development and use, drawing on 25 interviews with researchers and practitioners across industry, academia, civil society, and government. We find SOT are weakly integrated into AI governance processes, and identify two features of SOT design and use that explain why. First, the design choices through which SOT produce structured representations of the complex problem space of AI risks tend to be invisible to downstream taxonomy users. Those users treat the resulting categories as exhaustive accounts of risk rather than as interpretive aids. Second, SOT typically enumerate harms without linking them to decision points or actors implicated in their occurrence, leaving accountability difficult to assign. We close with design recommendations for SOT developers and users, and argue realising the potential of SOT requires governance infrastructure that does not yet exist.
papers.summary_zh: 该文基于对产业界、学术界、公民社会与政府部门研究者和实践者的访谈，考察AI风险分类体系（SOT）在治理实践中的开发与使用情况。研究发现，SOT与AI治理流程的整合较弱，原因有二：其设计选择对下游使用者不可见，使用者往往把分类当作穷尽性的风险清单而非解释性工具；同时SOT多列举危害，却未将其与决策节点和相关责任主体关联，导致问责难以落实。作者据此提出设计建议，并指出发挥SOT潜力尚需目前并不存在的治理基础设施。

papers.title: From Model Approval to Interface Governance: Federated Learning, Lifecycle Accountability, and AI-Enabled Software as a Medical Device
papers.authors: Ben Liu
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: AI-enabled Software as a Medical Device (AI-SaMD) is increasingly governed through lifecycle instruments such as predetermined change control plans and Good Machine Learning Practice. Federated learning has been advanced as a privacy-preserving alternative to centralized training, but it destabilizes a foundational assumption of medical device regulation: that governance can be attached to a discrete artifact. We argue that, under continuous cross-institutional adaptation, federated AI-SaMD cannot be governed as a model alone because responsibility becomes reconstructable only at institutional coordination boundaries. We develop interface governance as a necessary accountability layer for those boundaries. We make four contributions. We reconceptualize federated AI-SaMD as distributed clinical infrastructure and specify when an ordinary operational interaction becomes a formal governance interface: when clinically consequential risk, evidence, authority, or contestation moves across institutions and cannot be reconstructed from any single actor’s records. We then translate the framework into four minimal implementation conditions: standardized triggers, auditable logs, defined escalation routes, and institution-specific response duties. We also develop a patient-facing pathway for AI-involvement review, disclosure, and institutional response without requiring technical knowledge of federation. Interface governance does not replace existing regulatory mechanisms; it specifies the conditions under which they remain contestable, auditable, and actionable in federated clinical AI.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇理论论文，针对联邦学习使AI医疗软件（AI-SaMD）治理难以附着于单一模型的问题，提出“接口治理”作为必要的问责层。作者将联邦AI-SaMD重新界定为分布式临床基础设施，并说明当具有临床后果的风险、证据、权限或争议跨机构流动且无法由任一参与方记录重建时，日常操作交互即成为正式治理接口。文章据此提出标准化触发条件、可审计日志、明确的升级路径和机构特定的响应义务四项最低实施条件，并设计了面向患者的AI参与审查与披露路径；接口治理不替代现有监管机制，而是明确其在联邦临床AI中保持可争议、可审计和可行动的条件。

papers.title: CompanionSim: Synthetic Data for Evaluating Anthropomorphism in Human-AI Relationships
papers.authors: Jacy Reese Anthis, Mark Díaz, Renee Shelby
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Many people now see AI systems as not just productivity tools but as social companions. Researchers are eager to study the consequences of AI companionship behaviors, such as validation, which evoke trust, empathy, and attachment in human–human interaction. However, human–AI interaction data is limited and unreliable, slowing research progress. We scale small amounts of real-world data by simulating multi-turn human–chatbot dialogue across a range of chatbot behaviors and use cases. We release CompanionSim: a simulation framework with 2,240 simulated human–chatbot conversations representing 16 chatbot behaviors across seven use cases. Human participants annotated the simulated conversations and real-world conversations in two experiments probing perceptions of companionship behaviors. We conducted Study 1 with a U.S. representative sample (N = 628) and Study 2 across the U.S., U.K., India, and Nigeria (N = 3,646). Surprisingly, we find that companionship behaviors reduced likability, humanlikeness, and trust in AI chatbots. These effects were larger in particular subgroups: women and older participants saw companionship chatbots as less likable, humanlike, and trustworthy. We encourage researchers to leverage real-world and synthetic data together to study the differential impacts of AI companions and to create benchmark evaluations of AI chatbots.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对人机陪伴关系研究缺乏可靠交互数据的问题，构建了 CompanionSim 模拟框架，通过模拟多轮人机对话生成覆盖多种聊天机器人行为和使用场景的合成数据，并让人类参与者对模拟对话与真实对话进行标注比较。两项标注实验的结果显示，陪伴性行为反而降低了聊天机器人受喜爱、拟人化和可信赖的程度，且这一效应在女性与年长参与者中更为明显。作者据此建议将真实数据与合成数据结合使用，以考察 AI 陪伴的差异化影响并建立聊天机器人的基准评测。

papers.title: Culturally Situated AI Safety for Youth: Saudi Arabian Perspectives of Youth, Parents and Teachers
papers.authors: Aljawharah Alzahrani, Tanusree Sharma
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are widely used by youth and have introduced new privacy and safety challenges. While prior research has explored youth's safety in GenAI within a Western context, it often overlooks the cultural, religious, and social dimensions of technology use that strongly shape youth’s digital experiences in countries like Saudi Arabia. To address this gap, this study explores youth's (aged 7-17), parents' and teachers' interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through a non-Western lens. We analyzed 736 Reddit psots, and 1,262 X (Twitter) posts, and conducted interviews with 31 Saudi Arabian participants (8 youth, 13 parents, 10 teachers). Our findings highlight context-dependent and relational privacy and safety needs of GenAI use from non-Western context, which are often shaped by communal structure and prescribed norms. We found significant risks tied to youth’s disclosure of personal and family information, which conflict with culturally rooted expectations of modesty, privacy, and honor, particularly when youth seek emotional support from GenAI. These risks are further compounded by socio-economic factors such as cost-saving practices leading to the use of shared GenAI accounts (e.g., ChatGPT) within families or even among strangers. We provide design implications reflecting parents’ and teachers’ expectations of how youth should use GenAI. This work lays the groundwork for inclusive, context-sensitive parental controls that adhere to cultural norms and values.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注沙特阿拉伯青少年使用生成式人工智能时的隐私与安全风险，采用非西方文化视角，分析社交媒体帖文并对青少年、家长和教师进行访谈。研究发现，当地青少年的隐私与安全需求具有情境性和关系性，受集体结构与既定规范塑造；青少年向生成式AI透露个人和家庭信息、尤其寻求情感支持时，会与当地关于谦逊、隐私和荣誉的文化期待相冲突，而家庭甚至陌生人共用账号等节省成本的做法又加剧了这些风险。文章据此提出符合家长和教师期待的设计建议，为尊重文化规范的情境敏感型家长控制机制奠定基础。

papers.title: Bridging AI Research and Policy: A Co-Production Framework and the Case for Policy Transfer Offices
papers.authors: Malihe Alikhani, Jeongeun Kim, Anna Haensch, Saki Imai, Serena Booth, Andrea Stith, Adriana Bankston
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now shape governance, labor, healthcare, and public life at scale, yet there remains a persistent gap between technical knowledge and the policy processes meant to govern AI's use. We argue that this gap is not a communication failure but an institutional design problem: the absence of sustained, equitable mechanisms that make researcher-policymaker collaboration feasible. Drawing on theories of science-policy co-production, we present empirical evidence from a survey of AI researchers (n=44) that identifies the dominant structural barriers as time costs (66%), pathway opacity (57%), and weak institutional support, not lack of access to policymakers. We introduce a co-production framework centered on the novel proposal for Policy Transfer Offices (PTOs): institutional structures, analogous to technology transfer offices, that broker relationships, provide translation templates, and legitimize policy work within academic evaluation systems. We further expand on the proposal, in the dimensions of placement, governance, funding, and failure modes, and ground it in two in-depth case studies (algorithmic collusion and AI in education) that illustrate when technical expertise fails to reach governance in time, and what institutionalized co-production enables. We further analyze equity in participation, showing how current ad hoc models concentrate policy influence among senior researchers at elite institutions, and propose reforms for broadening access. The paper offers empirical evidence, an actionable institutional mechanism, and equity-centered design principles to align AI research with democratic governance.
papers.summary_zh: 该文指出人工智能研究与政策治理之间的鸿沟并非沟通问题，而是缺乏持续、公平的协作机制这一制度设计问题。作者基于对AI研究者的调查，发现时间成本、路径不透明和机构支持薄弱是主要结构性障碍，而非研究者接触不到政策制定者；据此提出以“政策转移办公室”为核心的共同生产框架，并通过算法合谋与AI教育两个案例说明技术专长未能及时进入治理的情形。文章还分析了当前临时性协作模式使政策影响力集中于资深研究者与精英机构，并给出扩大参与公平性的改革方向。

papers.title: AI Adoption Across a Multinational Workforce: Sociotechnical Conditions for GenAI Acceptance in Human Resources
papers.authors: Dalia Ali, Maria José Rodríguez Velázquez, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Vera Liao, Orestis Papakyriakopoulos
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) deployment in the workplace is accelerating rapidly. Nevertheless, questions of who adopts, who benefits, and who is left behind and why are still understudied. In this paper, we investigate these dynamics in the context of a multinational tech company transitioning from a legacy Human Resources (HR) search system to a GenAI-supported system, analyzing search log data, survey data (n=25), and ten semi-structured interviews. Our findings show that adoption depended on the fit between the GenAI system’s design assumptions and employees’ work positionalities (role, spoken language, tenure). Further, we find that employees’ trust in GenAI answers was built through source-checking, comparison among systems, and seeking input from colleagues or HR when in doubt. Our contribution is twofold. First, we provide empirical evidence of workplace GenAI adoption during a live organizational transition, showing that adoption is influenced by factors such as situational fit, search literacy, and trust calibration. It is also further shaped by knowledge conditions such as the system’s content quality, employee training, and guidance. Second, we translate these findings into design considerations for inclusive deployment and adoption in high-stakes environments such as HR. We argue that organizations should design systems considering the role and context-sensitive benefits they yield to different social groups. They also need to treat the organizational knowledge infrastructure as AI infrastructure to improve the accountability and usability of GenAI systems.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察一家跨国科技公司从传统人力资源检索系统转向生成式AI支持系统时，员工采纳的差异及其成因，分析结合了搜索日志、问卷和访谈数据。研究发现，采纳程度取决于系统设计假设与员工工作处境（角色、使用语言、任职时间）之间的契合度；员工对AI答案的信任则通过核查来源、比较不同系统以及向同事或HR求证来建立。作者据此提出，系统设计应顾及不同群体的角色与情境化收益，并将组织知识基础设施视为AI基础设施，以提升生成式AI系统的可问责性与可用性。

papers.title: On Seeding Watermarks to Detect Verbatim LLM Copy-Paste Responses
papers.authors: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Artin Yousefi, Robert Pless
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made fluent essay writing, code drafting, and quiz answering instantly available to students at every level, from secondary school through graduate study. Many educators do not object to LLM use per se; what they need to detect is the case in which a student pastes the assignment prompt into a chatbot and submits the model's reply verbatim, without engaging with the work. Existing post-hoc AI-text detectors remain unreliable and have been shown to penalise non-native English writers, while output-side watermarks require cooperation from the model provider. We propose an alternative that the educator controls directly: an input-side watermark in which an invisible instruction is embedded inside the visible assignment prompt itself. An LLM that ingests the prompt verbatim quietly reads the hidden instruction and writes a tell-tale signature into its reply, exposing the copy-and-paste pathway specifically. We describe SteganoPrompt, a single-page, zero-dependency web tool that encodes an arbitrary printable-ASCII payload into the deprecated Unicode Tags block (U+E0000--U+E007F). The encoded string is visually identical to the original, survives common copy-paste channels (Word, Google Docs, PDF, Markdown, Slack, e-mail, the major learning-management systems), and is tokenized as ordinary text by most frontier models. We evaluate compliance across eight LLM families and a representative set of educational content channels. To keep deployment transparent, disclosure is built into the tool itself: every encoded brief also carries a brief, always-on academic-integrity reminder for the student, and we set out concrete guidance recommending for its disclosed, ethical use in the classroom.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对学生将作业题目直接粘贴给大语言模型并原样提交回复这一具体场景，提出由教师直接掌控的输入端水印方案：在可见的作业题目中嵌入不可见指令，模型逐字读取题目后会在回复中留下可识别标记，从而暴露复制粘贴路径。作者实现了单页、零依赖的网页工具 SteganoPrompt，将任意可打印 ASCII 载荷编码进已弃用的 Unicode Tags 区块，编码后文本在视觉上与原文一致，可经受常见复制粘贴渠道，并被多数前沿模型按普通文本分词。研究在八个模型系列和一组代表性教育内容渠道上评估了合规情况，并在工具中内置学术诚信提醒，给出了公开、合乎伦理的课堂使用建议。需注意，该方案针对的是逐字复制粘贴，而非一般性的模型使用。

papers.title: Silent Updates: Measuring and Closing the Post-Deployment Disclosure Gap
papers.authors: Sophia Abraham, Ben Bucknall
papers.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI Ethics and Society
papers.abstract: Deployed foundation models are often not static systems, with providers able to modify system behavior through fine-tuning, classifier updates, system prompt revisions, retrieval changes, and routing changes. These updates can be made silently—that is, without public disclosure, a version increment, or re-evaluation. Such silent updates challenge a core assumption behind current AI governance frameworks that an externally verifiable chain of custody links the model referred to in evaluation results or a system card to the model served to users. In this paper, we examine post-deployment disclosure practices across first-party API providers and inference hosts to establish the extent to which a chain of custody exists in practice. We find that providers commonly publish substantial safety documentation, including quantitative evaluations and version-specific reports, but no provider in our sample published information allowing an external party to verify that the artifact being served is the same one referred to in this documentation. We introduce the Silent Updates Scorecard, a public instrument for measuring post-deployment disclosure practices across providers and hosts, and preliminary results for a sample of nine first-party API providers and seven third-party inference hosts. We also propose a Three-Part Behavioral Trigger System for determining when post-deployment modifications to a system motivate disclosure or re-evaluation obligations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察已部署基础模型在更新披露方面的实践缺口：模型提供方可通过微调、分类器更新、提示词修订、检索或路由调整等方式静默修改系统行为，而不做公开披露、版本递增或重新评估，这动摇了现有AI治理框架所依赖的“可外部核验的保管链”假设。作者通过梳理第一方API提供方与推理托管方的部署后披露实践，发现各方虽普遍发布大量安全文档（含量化评估与版本报告），但样本中没有任何一方提供可供外部核验所服务模型与文档所指模型一致的信息。文章据此提出用于衡量部署后披露实践的Silent Updates Scorecard，并给出对九家第一方API提供方和七家第三方推理托管方的初步结果，同时提出一个三部分行为触发系统，用以判断何时部署后修改应触发披露或重新评估义务。

papers.title: Human–AI collaborative patterns in GenAI-supported instructional design among pre-service teachers: an analysis of interaction sequences and cognitive load
papers.authors: Xu Fang, Junci Feng, Bianyu Yan, Binbin Zhou
papers.journal: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the paradigm of instructional design. However, the micro-level process patterns of human-AI collaboration in generative AI-enabled instructional design for pre-service teachers still require in-depth analysis. This study aims to uncover the behavioral patterns and cognitive load characteristics of pre-service teachers when collaborating with generative AI to complete instructional design tasks and to explore the patterns of efficient human-AI collaboration. A total of 67 pre-service teachers completed instructional design tasks with AI assistance. A systematic instructional plan quality evaluation rubric was developed based on relevant theories, and participants were assigned to the high-quality and low-quality groups using a median split of their lesson-plan quality scores. The study employed lag sequential analysis to compare the behavioral sequence patterns between the two groups and measured their multidimensional cognitive load. The results indicate that the high-quality group exhibited a significant evaluation-revision bidirectional cycle and a revision self-loop, with a clear progressive sequence of “planning → decision-making → generation → evaluation → revision → re-evaluation” in their behavioral flow. In contrast, the low-quality group was mired in ineffective cycles, with fragmented behavioral logic. Key findings showed large effect sizes for the evaluation-revision cycle ( r = 0.606) and for mental demand ( r = 0.647). Regarding cognitive load, the high-quality group reported no greater subjective effort than the low-quality group (though this null finding should be interpreted with caution given the study’s power limitations). A second round of within-sample replication confirmed that these core findings were consistent across a second task. Based on the human-AI collaborative behavioral patterns and cognitive load of the high-quality and low-quality groups, the study constructed a model of the human-AI collaboration patterns in generative AI-enabled instructional design for pre-service teachers. Specifically, higher-quality outputs were associated with a pattern oriented toward cognitive efficiency, characterised by deep processing (evaluation-revision iteration) and by the avoidance of ineffective cycles. Conversely, lower-quality outputs co-occurred with ineffective cycles arising in the context of interaction obstacles, in which repeated clarifications and interrupted revisions were accompanied by higher cognitive and emotional load, describing a pattern of high investment with low output. Because participants were grouped on the basis of their design outcomes, these findings are correlational and do not establish the direction of the relationships; they nonetheless provide empirical evidence to inform the optimisation of human-AI collaboration in GenAI-supported instructional design.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注职前教师与生成式人工智能协作完成教学设计时的微观行为模式与认知负荷特征，通过让参与者借助AI完成设计任务，并依据教案质量分组，比较两组的行为序列与多维认知负荷。结果显示，高质量组表现出“评估—修改”的双向循环与修改自循环，行为流呈现从规划、决策、生成到评估、修改、再评估的递进顺序；低质量组则陷入无效循环，行为逻辑较为碎片化。高质量组的心理需求得分关联较强，但其主观努力并未高于低质量组，作者提示这一零结果受统计功效限制需谨慎解读。研究据此构建了人智协同教学设计模式，指出更高质量产出与深度迭代、避免无效循环的认知效率取向相关，而低质量产出则与互动障碍下的反复澄清和中断修改相伴随。由于按设计结果分组，这些发现属于相关关系，不能确定因果方向。

papers.title: How Generative AI-Assisted Formative Feedback Is Appraised and Implemented in Online Collaborative Learning
papers.authors: Guoqing Lu, Huimin Zhang, Shen Ba, Lan Yang
papers.abstract: Effective educational feedback is vital for enhancing student learning, yet providing personalized formative feedback in large-class settings remains challenging. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) offers a potential means of scaling formative feedback. Guided by a self-determination theory-based model, this study examines the features, implementation, and pre-service teachers’ perceptions of generative AI-assisted formative feedback (GAI-FF) at a university in China. Participants ( n = 114) received four types of GAI-FF, varying in complexity and focus, across three feedback intervals during a semester. Feedback content and written reflections were analyzed using content analysis, epistemic network analysis, and thematic analysis. Results indicate that (1) GAI can generate formative feedback with distinct cognitive and affective feature patterns; (2) overall implementation of GAI-FF was limited; (3) feedback containing problem identification, suggestions, and solutions was more likely to be enacted, whereas feedback emphasizing affective features was less frequently implemented; and (4) participants expressed mixed perceptions, recognizing the usefulness of GAI-FF for collaborative learning while also noting constraints related to rigidity, accuracy, and practical applicability. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of GAI-FF depends on how it supports learners’ cognitive, motivational, and affective appraisals, which shape subsequent feedback use. The study also highlights the importance of deliberate instructional design and cautious integration of GAI tools in formative assessment practices.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于自我决定理论模型，考察在线协作学习中职前教师对生成式人工智能形成性反馈（GAI-FF）的感知与实施情况，参与者在一学期内分三个反馈间隔收到复杂度与侧重点不同的四类反馈，研究对反馈内容和书面反思进行了内容分析、认知网络分析与主题分析。结果显示，GAI 能生成在认知与情感特征上具有不同模式的反馈，但反馈的整体实施程度有限；包含问题识别、建议与解决方案的反馈更易被采纳，而侧重情感特征的反馈实施较少。参与者对 GAI-FF 的感知褒贬不一，既认可其对协作学习的用处，也指出僵化、准确性和实际适用性方面的局限。研究据此认为，GAI-FF 的效果取决于其如何支持学习者的认知、动机与情感评价，并强调在形成性评价中需有意识地设计教学并审慎整合 GAI 工具。

papers.title: Between Human and Machine: University Teachers’ Accounts of Judgment, Metacognitive Defense, and Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI Use
papers.authors: Zhen Qiang, Zhuo Wang
